title: 🚗 A Driverless Taxi Finally on the Streets of San Francisco — "Uber", "Lucid" and "Nuro" Begin Full Testing
body: 🚗 A Driverless Taxi Finally on the Streets of San Francisco — "Uber", "Lucid" and "Nuro" Begin Full Testing
The companies "Uber", "Lucid" and "Nuro" announced on Tuesday the start of testing fully driverless taxis on public roads in the San Francisco Bay Area, with no safety driver behind the wheel.

Electric "Lucid Gravity" cars, fitted with "Nuro"'s self-driving system, are now driving through the cities of Palo Alto, Mountain View, Los Altos and Sunnyvale, expanding to other cities in the area over the coming year.

The companies had been testing the same cars since last December, but with a human driver ready to step in; now the car drives itself entirely, after "Nuro" received a driverless testing permit from California's Department of Motor Vehicles last May.

The car carries high-resolution cameras, "lidar" devices and radars that build a complete picture of the road around it, and "Lucid" has delivered more than 100 cars equipped with the latest hardware and software in preparation for the new phase.

Employee rides in the driverless cars are set to begin soon, paving the way for a public launch in the first quarter of 2027 through the "Uber" app, which has committed to buying at least 20,000 cars over six years.
Simply put: a taxi that reaches you with no driver, opens the door for you by itself and drives you to your destination on its own; the real test now is in streets crowded with people and cars.
Would you ride in a driverless taxi if it came to your city?
